# Attempt to read property "email" on int - Laravel 8 Encountering a PHP error stating `Attempt to read property "email" on int` during development is a classic symptom of accessing an object property without first instantiating that object. In the context of your specific scenario, this error occurs because `$i->requestor_id` returns an integer (the primary key) rather than a `User` model instance. This discrepancy stems from how Laravel resolves relationships and how eager loading interacts with relationship accessor naming conventions. The root cause lies in the definition of your relationship within the `Work` model. You have defined the method as `requestor_id()`: ```php public function requestor_id() { return $this->hasOne(User::class); } ``` When you access `$obra->requestor_id`, Laravel invokes this method and returns a new `User` instance containing the data for that specific user. However, if you do not use eager loading via the `with()` clause in your query builder or Eloquent model scope, Laravel loads the relationship lazily. If the relationship does not exist or is null, accessing it directly on the collection item might behave unexpectedly depending on the version and specific configuration, but more critically, accessing `$obra->requestor_id` when using a custom accessor name often confuses developers regarding what data is being retrieved. In your view blade syntax, you are attempting to chain access: `{{ $i->requestor_id->email }}`. For this to work, `$i->requestor_id` must resolve to an object with an `email` property. If the error says it is reading on an `int`, it implies that `$i->requestor_id` is returning the ID instead of the model. This usually happens when you are trying to access a relationship without eager loading, and Laravel optimizes the query or the relationship definition causes a fallback behavior where the accessor returns the foreign key if the relation isn't found, though strictly speaking, `hasOne` should return an instance or null. The most robust solution is to ensure the data is loaded before iterating over the collection. You can achieve this by modifying your controller logic to eager load the relationship explicitly: ```php $obras = Obra::with('requestor_id')->get(); return view("obra.index", compact("obras")); ``` By calling `with('requestor_id')`, you instruct Eloquent to perform a single SQL query that joins the `works` table with the `users` table, ensuring that every `$i->requestor_id` inside your loop is fully hydrated as a `User` model instance. This prevents lazy loading issues and guarantees that accessing `$i->requestor_id->email` will retrieve the string value from the `email` column in the database rather than triggering an error on an integer ID. Alternatively, if you prefer to keep the relationship definition strictly adhering to Laravel's default naming conventions, you could rename your accessor in the model to match the foreign key name exactly, such as changing `requestor_id()` to just `requestor()`. This aligns with standard Eloquent practices where the method name matches the relation name without the `_id` suffix. However, keeping a custom name like `requestor_id` is valid provided you always eager load it or handle null checks in your view logic. Another approach involves using dot notation directly in the Blade template to access nested properties, which can sometimes simplify syntax, though it does not solve the underlying issue if the relationship itself isn't loaded: ```blade
  • {{ $i->requestor_id?.email }}
    • ``` The nullsafe operator (`?`) added here would prevent the crash by returning an empty string if the relationship is null, but it would still return `int` errors if the property exists on an integer. Therefore, eager loading remains the definitive fix for performance and correctness. If you are dealing with a large dataset where eager loading might impact memory usage significantly due to the size of the join, consider implementing pagination or filtering before loading the full relationship data. For further reading on optimizing Eloquent queries and understanding relationship accessors in depth, resources like https://laravelcompany.com provide detailed insights into best practices for handling collections and relationships efficiently in your application architecture.
